title: U.S. House · Montana's 2nd District
area: Eastern Montana, including Billings and Great Falls.

context.text: Incumbent Rep. Troy Downing (R) did not face a primary challenger in 2026, winning renomination unopposed.

summary.text: Troy Downing is the Republican incumbent seeking a second term in Montana's 2nd Congressional District. A technology and insurance entrepreneur and Air Force and Air National Guard veteran, he served as Montana State Auditor from 2021 to 2025 before his election to the U.S. House in 2024. He serves on the House Financial Services Committee.

background.text: Raised in Indio, California; studied computer science at New York University, where, according to his official biography, he worked as a research scientist and teacher in the university's IT department.

Co-founded WebCal, an internet-based calendar system incorporated into Yahoo in 1998, and moved to Montana after its sale; his official biography says he later mentored and financed other startups as an angel investor.

Enlisted in the U.S. Air Force and Air National Guard after the September 11, 2001 attacks, serving eight years with a Combat Search and Rescue squadron (the 129th Rescue Squadron, per Ballotpedia) with two tours in Afghanistan.
Was CEO of AC Self Storage Solutions, operated a commercial real estate development firm, and founded a commercial insurance company.
Ran unsuccessfully in the 2018 Republican primary for U.S. Senate in Montana.

Won the 2020 election for Montana Commissioner of Securities and Insurance (State Auditor), after defeating two opponents in the Republican primary, and served from 2021 to 2025; in that role he also sat on the state Board of Land Commissioners.
Won the 2nd Congressional District seat in 2024 and took office on January 3, 2025; he sits on the House Financial Services Committee.

Remains involved with Montana veterans' organizations; Ballotpedia lists him as a member of the Montana Veterans of Foreign Wars and a volunteer with the Warriors and Quiet Waters Foundation. His official biography says he lives in Helena with his wife, Heather, and they have four grown children.

priorities.text: Supports making the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act permanent and has introduced legislation aimed at expanding rural small businesses' access to capital.

Supports an "all-of-the-above" energy approach that emphasizes coal, oil and gas production in Montana, including legislation to keep the Bull Mountains coal mine open and to support Signal Peak's mining operations.

positions.summary: Supports making the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act's lower tax rates permanent and has cosponsored repeal of the federal estate tax.
Says fossil fuels are an abundant, cost-efficient energy source and supports coal, oil and gas production over restrictions aimed at reducing emissions.
Supports reducing federal involvement in education and says parents are best suited to make educational choices for their children.

record.text: Sits on the House Financial Services Committee and the Small Business Committee (Innovation, Entrepreneurship, and Workforce Development; and Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.
Introduced the Federal Insurance Office Elimination Act to eliminate the Federal Insurance Office.

Introduced the Expanding Access to Capital for Rural Job Creators Act, which would require the SEC's Office of the Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation to identify capital-access challenges facing rural small businesses.

candidates.name: Brian Miller
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary with 55.5% of the vote over Sam Lux and Jonathan Windy Boy (who unofficially withdrew).

summary.text: Brian Miller is the Democratic nominee for Montana's 2nd Congressional District. A Helena attorney originally from Florida who has lived in Montana since the late 1990s, he handles civil cases for small businesses, consumers and individuals. He won the June 2 Democratic primary.

background.text: Is originally from Florida and has lived in Montana since the late 1990s.

Has practiced law in Helena since at least 2010 with the firm Morrison, Sherwood, Wilson and Deola, and runs a private practice handling civil cases for small businesses, consumers and other individuals against insurance companies, banks and others.
Has two children, whom he told the Glendive Ranger-Review are his greatest motivation for running.
Launched his campaign in late 2025 and won the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary, defeating Sam Lux and state Sen. Jonathan Windy Boy, who had suspended his campaign.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Candidate Connection survey response, or other public statements found for Brian Miller in the time available.

candidates.name: Patrick McCracken
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed after the Libertarian primary was canceled.

summary.text: Patrick McCracken is the Libertarian Party nominee for Montana's 2nd Congressional District. A financial advisor by background, he describes himself as a fourth-generation Montanan and is running on cost of living, health insurance and food prices.

background.text: Says he is 48, has lived in Montana his whole life as a fourth-generation Montanan, graduated from Billings West High School and attended school in Bozeman.

Worked as a financial advisor for about 10 years, left the state for work for a period, and says he has spent roughly 20 years or more helping people with their financial planning, now in a work-from-home job.

Became the Libertarian nominee without a primary opponent after the June 2, 2026 Libertarian primary was canceled; he is from Columbia Falls and mentions his wife and kids in a Montana Public Radio interview.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Candidate Connection survey response, or other public statements found for Patrick McCracken in the time available.

candidates.name: Michael Eisenhauer

summary.text: Michael (Mike) Eisenhauer is an independent candidate for Montana's 2nd Congressional District. A cardiologist from Great Falls who spent about 25 years in the U.S. Army as a physician and health care administrator, he says he is running to represent voters in the political middle.

background.text: Is 62 and grew up in Nebraska, according to KPAX.
Spent about 25 years in the U.S. Army as a physician and health care administrator, then moved to Wyoming.
Moved to Great Falls about 10 years ago and worked as a cardiologist with Benefis Health System; describes himself as semi-retired and working as a traveling physician serving smaller facilities.
Is running as an independent, which required gathering petition signatures from registered voters to qualify for the general election ballot, and is on the November 3 ballot.
